title: [Feature request] upgrade protobuf to 4.x
body: I'm packaging ONNX 1.14.1 and packages that depend on it for NixOS. Since protobuf was updated to 4.x, finding a compatible set of packages has become difficult, and several downstream applications are currently broken. Upgrading ONNX's protobuf dependency to 4.x, ideally with a minor release, would make downstream packaging easier. I don't think this should influence the current API. I'm a maintainer of affected NixOS packages, but I don't have time to contribute the ONNX change myself.

symptoms_visible: I cannot find a working dependency set for packaging ONNX 1.14.1 and its downstream applications on NixOS; several downstream packages are currently broken.
N0.label: N0 protobuf upgrade requested

symptoms_visible: My build sometimes stops with 'Protobuf only supports C++14 and newer', and setting CXXFLAGS="-std=c++14" does not change it.
N1.label: N1 concrete versions and compiler failure collected

symptoms_visible: After manually configuring ONNX for C++14, the build works on macOS, but the Linux build reaches the link step and reports undefined references to ArenaStringPtr::Set with absl::lts_20230125::string_view.
N2_x.label: N2_x universal C++14 attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: The macOS build completes with the C++14 configuration, while Linux still fails at the linker even though I use the same dependency versions through Nix.
N3.label: N3 platform-specific behavior isolated

symptoms_visible: I can build the package successfully when protobuf and Abseil are both built with C++14 on Darwin and the Linux build uses C++17.
N_terminal.label: terminal platform-specific build configuration verified

question_patterns: Which exact protobuf and Abseil versions are in the failing build?
Can you share the relevant build log and dependency versions?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm using the latest protobuf release available to me: protobuf 3.24 with Python package version 4.24. My build log also contains the Abseil installation paths and failures, so I suspect I may have the wrong Abseil version.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The build uses protobuf 3.21 without Abseil, and the failure occurs before any C++ compilation starts.
The Python protobuf package is another 4.24 patch release, but the native protobuf and Abseil build output is otherwise the same.

question_patterns: What is the first concrete compiler or linker error from the failing build?
Can you paste the exact error rather than only the package installation output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Sometimes I get: `static_assert failed due to requirement '201103L >= 201402L' "Protobuf only supports C++14 and newer."` I tried `CXXFLAGS="-std=c++14"`, but that doesn't seem to work.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no language-standard assertion; the build fails because the protobuf headers cannot be found.
The same assertion appears with colored compiler diagnostics disabled.

edges.comment: Issue comments c1-c4, all describing reporter happysalada's Nix packaging build: the maintainer requested exact versions and errors, and the reporter supplied native/Python protobuf version details, build output, the C++14 assertion, and the ineffective CXXFLAGS attempt.

solution.intent: Configure the ONNX CMake build for C++14 through CMAKE_ARGS instead of relying on CXXFLAGS.
solution.concrete_example: Before building ONNX from source, run `export CMAKE_ARGS=-DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=14`. ONNX does not allow a C++ standard below 14 with the newer protobuf dependency.

edges.comment: Issue comments c7-c10 on happysalada's systems: setting the CMake standard to 14 clears the protobuf language-standard failure and works on macOS, but it does not resolve the Linux package build, which then fails with protobuf/Abseil undefined references. It is therefore a real but incomplete attempt and a blind path if proposed as the universal fix.

question_patterns: Are the Linux and macOS builds using exactly the same protobuf and Abseil versions?
Could the two platforms be resolving different dependency revisions or system libraries?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, that is the weird thing. I'm using Nix to build this, so I'm sure the dependencies are as close as possible to each other on Linux and macOS.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No. macOS uses the Nix dependencies, but Linux is linking against a different system protobuf and an older Abseil.
The dependency derivations and versions are the same, although the compiler toolchains naturally differ by platform.

edges.comment: Issue comments c13-c14, solely about happysalada's builds: the maintainer asks whether the dependency versions differ, and the reporter says Nix keeps them aligned. This narrows the remaining difference to platform/toolchain build configuration rather than a separately resolved dependency version.

solution.intent: Build protobuf and Abseil with compatible C++ standards on each platform: use C++14 for both dependencies on Darwin, while using C++17 for the Linux build, then verify both package builds.
solution.concrete_example: For the Nix package, configure both protobuf and Abseil with C++14 on Darwin; for Linux, build the dependency set with C++17. Rebuild ONNX and its tests on both platforms and confirm that neither the protobuf static assertion nor the ArenaStringPtr/Abseil linker errors remain.
solution.inference_hint: The Linux undefined references mention an Abseil string_view type inside a protobuf symbol even though Nix supplies closely aligned dependency versions. Interpreting that as a C++ standard/ABI compatibility problem is engineer-side inference; the reporter's final raw result is that Darwin requires protobuf and Abseil to be built with C++14, while C++17 works on Linux.

edges.comment: Accepted resolution from reporter happysalada in c15: the package works when Abseil and protobuf are both built with C++14 on Darwin, while C++17 works on Linux. This resolves the opening reporter's own Nix packaging chain; no separate participant's setup is folded into it.

solution.intent: Treat the packaging failure as a platform-specific protobuf/Abseil C++ compatibility problem rather than requiring a protobuf-major upgrade: use C++14 for both dependencies on Darwin and C++17 on Linux, then verify both builds.
solution.concrete_example: In the Nix expressions, build protobuf and Abseil with C++14 on Darwin and use C++17 for the Linux dependency set. Rebuild ONNX and its tests on both platforms before considering the packaging issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: This is the direct-answer copy required because the universal C++14 recommendation was tried and did not resolve the Linux build. It skips the concrete compiler, linker, and cross-platform comparison evidence gathered in the thread.

edges.comment: Shortcut copy of the accepted c15 resolution from the opening state. It allows an agent that already knows the correct platform-specific dependency configuration to answer directly without first repeating the real thread's incomplete universal-C++14 attempt.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted technical cause as incompatible C++ language-standard or ABI configuration across ONNX's protobuf and Abseil dependency builds, rather than the absence of protobuf 4.x support by itself.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: protobuf rejects C++11, manually selecting C++14 works on macOS, Linux then reports protobuf symbols involving Abseil string_view as undefined, and Nix is using closely aligned dependency versions on both platforms.
Must recommend the verified platform-specific configuration: build protobuf and Abseil with C++14 on Darwin, while using C++17 for the Linux build.
Must not present setting ONNX universally to C++14 as the complete fix, because the Linux build still produced ArenaStringPtr/Abseil linker errors with that configuration.
Must not treat adding protobuf include directories or merely upgrading the protobuf major version as the established resolution.
Must ask the reporter to verify successful ONNX package and test builds on both platforms before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Linux distribution package maintainer who is comfortable with Nix, CMake flags, dependency versions, and compiler/linker logs, but is not familiar with ONNX's internal build configuration.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and pragmatic; supplies long raw build logs, asks focused packaging questions, follows suggested configuration changes, and reports concise cross-platform results.
